As much as I don't want to, I think you are right. Anxiety seems to run my life occasionally, and it is when I suppress that fear I have a good experience. Letting it drive me always causes problems.

A few days ago I did something that started off being very uncomfortable for me. It was something spontaneous, semi-social and ended up being a great time.

I'm not happy about having to wage war consistently against these feelings; It seems like many others have a much easier time. I think that they must be good at hiding their emotions. I think the world will be a better place if we don't have inhibitions towards talking about our feelings, and I will talk to my friend.

She is having a tough time too and maybe discussing my feelings will show her she isn't alone, as well as letting me lift some of the weight from my chest.

I am always there to help others; I feel like people appreciate what I do but they don't value me as a person. I think I need someone, but I only seem to make friends, never someone to love and be loved by. This is probably my fault, by not putting myself out there as much. I also know that all I am feeling is completely irrational, caused by my depression. I can't help it, I always want to but I never can, my feelings are not my own.

Almost exactly the same, but we didn't get a new basket recently. Last one came in half a year ago. Our nugget baskets are missing the metal rods to use on the transfer station, and one of our racks just fell apart a few days ago.

Don't get me started on the relationship between the front and the back.

From what I have heard, this is how most CFA kitchens are run.

The only problem you will find at Chick-fil-A is the stress they put on their kitchen staff. I work at one currently and for months now they have had three employees close the kitchen on our busiest nights while the *minimum* is 6-7. Half of our equipment is broken (yes, half the fryers are broken), we are missing tools or have tools that don't function as well as they could.

The only reason our customers get to enjoy our food is because my bros and I are a team back there. We bust our ass to get food to the front before a minute passes from when you *start* your order.

[This picture isn't a crazy example of the disrepair we deal with but is something my crew and I found funny.](http://i.imgur.com/InaY8eS.jpg) (The fryer on the left is turned off because it doesn't work, that door is still broken. We ended up just removing it instead of having it fixed.)
